title: How It All Started (and Almost Didn’t)
excerpt: Nexubis launched in May 2023, initially operating as a behind-the-scenes white-label Webflow agency built on founder relationships. Soul-crushing invisibility led to a strategic shift: prioritizing direct client partnerships and retainers over ghost work. Key hires, expanding services like in-house 3D/motion, and learning that referrals beat expensive marketing agencies fueled growth. By late 2024, we hit R2.2 million revenue, secured major retainers, and built sustainable systems.
author: Hannes Oosthuizen
bodyHtml:
I didn’t plan on building a company. Not seriously.

I had a solid gig, a Creative Director role lined up, and all the “right next steps” laid out. But something in me knew it was time. Not time to climb — time to build.

So I jumped.

I registered Nexubis on May 23rd, 2023. I dropped the public announcement a few weeks before. And then, ironically enough, my previous employer became my first client. Full-circle moment. First retainer signed. A bit of runway secured. Game on.

The Early Days: Hustle, Hide, Repeat

In the beginning, Nexubis was a white-label Webflow agency. We were behind-the-scenes muscle for other agencies — shipping fast, staying invisible, and collecting invoice payments like good little freelancers.

It paid the bills. But it killed the soul a little.

We weren’t allowed to show the work. No portfolio. No proof. No brand equity.

It felt like ghostwriting a bestseller… and not getting your name on the cover.

The Network That Built the Business

I leaned hard on relationships I’d built in past roles — ex-HODs, marketers, board members. They threw us bones, then real projects, then long-term retainers.

That’s when momentum started showing up. Real brands. Real credit. We were building something — not just billing hours.

We picked up another retainer shortly after. Then a few side gigs. Then the first taste of “we should probably hire someone” panic.

So we did. We hired.

Our first full-time team member joined in Jan 2024. We were still mostly white-label at that point, with a few direct clients in the mix. But I knew this wasn’t sustainable. We needed retainers, relationships, and stability — not just gigs that ended when someone’s roadmap shifted.

Then, things clicked.

The First Big Break (That Didn’t Come From an Ad Campaign)

We got introduced to a company that would become one of our biggest retainers to date. Not through marketing. Not through paid ads. Through a referral — the oldest, most underrated growth hack of all time.

We delivered, fast and clean, and suddenly, we had breathing room. That opened the door to hiring again. People I’d always wanted to work with. People who got the vision. People who raised the bar.

We brought in a proper Ops Manager. No more soloing the admin, chasing invoices, juggling projects, and running Slack all at once. (Kind of wild it took me this long to hand over internal responsibilities — but hey, trust issues die slow.)

And just like that, we weren’t just “a Webflow agency” anymore. We were Nexubis.

The Shift

Here’s the thing: white-label work paid the bills, but it was never ours.

It didn’t build the brand. It didn’t grow our credibility. And when one job ended, there was no guarantee another was coming. So I made the call — less white-label, more partnerships. Less one-off, more retainer. Less ghost work, more real brand-building.

And that meant expanding what we could offer.

Clients started asking for 3D visuals, motion, animation. We were outsourcing it — expensive, slow, inconsistent. So we brought it in-house. And it changed everything.

With that, we started standing out. We became the agency that could do more — cleaner, faster, better. That reputation snowballed. We landed bigger clients, bigger brands, and — eventually — a few big names I’d once dreamed of working with.

Lessons (Some Expensive)

Not everything was a win.

I once hired a marketing company to help us scale. Big retainer, slick pitch, zero results. Three months, down the drain. Expensive lesson: not everyone who says they can help you grow actually can. That’s when I realized — the best growth? It came from doing great work and getting referred.

Simple. Old-school. Still undefeated.

The Numbers

By the end of 2024:

  • We’d added 4 team members
  • Pulled in over R2.2 million in revenue
  • Landed 4 major retainers
  • Built systems that didn’t rely on chaos and caffeine
  • Started getting referrals faster than we could say yes

2025 kicked off with two more hires — a hybrid designer/dev and our first intern — and then another growth spurt. New clients, new markets, new systems. It was clear we needed someone focused just on scale. So we brought in a COO to help lead the next phase.

And now?

We’ve had the best two months in Nexubis history.
We’re running lean, shipping fast, and saying no to the wrong stuff.
We’re focused — not just on building cool things, but building the right things with the right people.

Final Thought

Nexubis didn’t start with a deck. Or a seed round. Or a 10-year roadmap.

It started with a “f*ck it, let’s build” moment.

And that’s what this series — Founders Diary — is here to document.
Not the highlight reel. Not the investor pitch.
The real stories. The messy ones. The wins, the failures, and the calls that either made us… or almost broke us.

More to come.

title: Circuit: Securing Nexubis
excerpt: We first met Circuit back when the rooms were smaller, the coffee stronger, and “five-minute chats” somehow turned into midnight presentations. The kind of early-stage chaos you weirdly miss later. They didn’t just open the door; they kept it open. This one’s about them first. How they build, how they collaborate, and how working with Circuit didn’t just level up our output, it leveled up how Nexubis thinks.
author: Hannes Oosthuizen
bodyHtml:
We first met Circuit back when the rooms were smaller, the coffee stronger, and “five-minute chats” somehow turned into midnight presentations. The kind of early-stage chaos you weirdly miss later. They didn’t just open the door; they kept it open. This one’s about them first. How they build, how they collaborate, and how working with Circuit didn’t just level up our output, it leveled up how Nexubis thinks.

‍

What Circuit Actually Does

Circuit builds Automatic Asset Extraction, a recovery system designed to mitigate issues that may arise in crypto and custody. If keys are lost, a custodian fails, or a wallet gets compromised, Circuit moves assets to safety on purpose, not on hope. It’s a shift from key-centric to asset-centric security. In simple terms: lose the keys, not the assets. That one line changed how we looked at security and how we designed everything around it.

‍

The Collaboration That Shaped Us

Initially, our brief was straightforward: refine the brand and streamline the website. But the deeper we went, the more complex the puzzle became. Circuit isn’t your average Web3 startup. They work at the intersection of regulation, infrastructure, and speed. So the challenge wasn’t to make them look good, it was to make them understood by compliance teams, executives, and engineers all at once. We rebuilt the system from the inside out: language, visuals, structure, all pointing to a single outcome: clarity under pressure.

‍

How Circuit Empowers Others

Circuit has this quiet confidence. They don’t gatekeep knowledge. They share context, connect the right people, and make sure the message lands, whether you’re a COO, a compliance officer, or a developer debugging on a Tuesday afternoon. Plug in their recovery pattern and your worst day becomes manageable. Not easy, but simple. There’s a difference.

‍

How They Helped Nexubis Grow

Phase one was small. We wanted to earn our seat at the table. We restructured their brand, refined investor decks, and redesigned the website to make complex recovery mechanics feel simple, fast, and credible. Then came funding. Then came scale. Suddenly, we were designing motion systems, 3D visual frameworks, and technical diagrams reviewed by people who had built security at global scale. We even collaborated with Yelena, the former CMO of Fireblocks, to refine how we communicated triggers, risk states, and failovers. Those sessions changed the way we think about storytelling in high-pressure industries, and that perspective has stayed with us since.

What We Built Together

  • A principle-driven brand system built to scale, not just look pretty
  • A website that translates complex recovery logic into a 10-second elevator pitch
  • A 3D and motion library that visualises cause, effect, and recovery with zero fluff
  • Investor and partner decks that link guarantees directly to business impact
  • Product UI design support that brings clarity where it matters most

We learned how to communicate trust visually, and that’s no small skill.

‍

The Hard Problem We Solved

Recovery in Web3 doesn’t have a common visual language. One bad metaphor and you risk overselling or confusing everything. Together, we refined that language. We stripped the noise. Used fewer words. Built motion that educates, not decorates. Every element, from product truth to visuals to tone, pointed in one direction: understanding.

‍

The Founder Behind The Mission

Harry is the kind of founder you want in your corner. Sharp, calm, collaborative, and allergic to ego. Working with him never felt like “take the brief and smile.” It felt like co-building. Like being part of something that genuinely matters. He brings that same energy to everyone he works with. You can feel it in the partners, the product, and even the Slack messages at 11 p.m.

‍

A Few Moments That Stuck

Some of our best moments were the smallest ones. Redrawing a single diagram three times until the failure path made sense in five seconds. Debating one verb because the wrong one might oversell the promise. Circuit didn’t just sign off on files; they shaped the thinking behind them. That kind of trust leaves a mark.

‍

Press And Proof

  • Forbes: Featured for redefining recovery architecture post-hack
  • SEC Crypto Task Force: Invited to roundtables on custody and risk language
  • Shift Markets Integration: Recovery by Default included in institutional trading flows

Each step proved that recovery doesn’t have to be reactive. It can be proactive, precise, and predictable.

‍

Gratitude

To Harry, Yelena, and the entire Circuit team, thank you. For the honest debates, the after-hours reverts, the patience, and the partnership that helped shape not just your brand, but ours too. Circuit didn’t just help secure assets. They helped secure our standards.

‍
